🩺 You took medical or nursing coursework, worked as a clinic assistant or grew up helping in a family doctor's practice.

🌱 Anatomy, diagnosis, medications and doses, wound care. You can recognize shock or a concussion and assist a doctor.
⚠️ Surgery, rare conditions and Quirk-linked illness are beyond you.
⚖️ You are not a licensed doctor or nurse; treating patients on your own authority or prescribing is illegal.
🏫 It shows in clinical vocabulary and steady attention at a bedside.

📈 Grants: Medicine +15
Studied: Medicine.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has studied medicine: anatomy, common illnesses, diagnosis from symptoms, medications and doses, wound care and how hospitals run. They can explain an injury, recognize shock or a concussion and assist a doctor. Prior study, not mastery: surgery, rare conditions and Quirk-linked illness are beyond them. Not a license: they are not a licensed doctor or nurse; treating patients on their own authority or prescribing is illegal. It shows in clinical vocabulary and steady attention at a bedside.

Studied: Science.name: Studied: Science
Studied: Science.description:
🔬 You studied the sciences: physics, chemistry and biology, a lab internship or an introductory Quirk science course.

🌱 You can estimate forces, identify a chemical hazard, run a careful experiment and reason about how a Quirk might work.
⚠️ Research-level Quirk genetics, restricted studies and advanced lab work are beyond you.
⚖️ It gives no lab access and no right to experiment on people; Quirk experiments on people without consent are a serious crime.
🏫 It shows in careful measurements, hypotheses spoken aloud and a lab notebook.

📈 Grants: Science +15
Studied: Science.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has studied science: physics, chemistry, biology and the basics of Quirk science, including how Quirks are inherited and why they vary. They can estimate forces, identify a chemical hazard, run a careful experiment and reason about how a Quirk might work. Prior study, not mastery: research-level Quirk genetics, restricted studies and advanced lab work are beyond them. Not a license: it gives no lab access and no right to experiment on people; Quirk experiments on people without consent are a serious crime. It shows in careful measurements, hypotheses spoken aloud and a lab notebook.

Studied: Academics.name: Studied: Academics
Studied: Academics.description:
📚 You were a strong student: entrance exam prep, cram school and top grades in math, literature and history.

🌱 Lectures, papers and written exams come more easily to you than to most.
⚠️ Specialist academy work still takes effort, and book learning says little about people.
⚖️ Grades open doors but promise nothing, and a scholarship can be lost.
🏫 It shows in neat notes, a study schedule and classmates asking to borrow your notes.

📈 Grants: Academics +15
Studied: Academics.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has studied hard: mathematics, modern and classical Japanese, history, the habits of a good student and the stamina for written exams. Lectures, papers and tests come more easily to them than to most. Prior study, not mastery: specialist academy work still takes effort, and book learning says little about people. Not a license: grades open doors but promise nothing, and a scholarship can be lost. It shows in neat notes, a study schedule and classmates who ask to borrow their notes.

Studied: Business.name: Studied: Business
Studied: Business.description:
💼 You studied business: commerce classes, keeping the books for a family shop or managing a store's accounts part-time.

🌱 Budgets, contracts, marketing and how hero agencies make money. You can read a balance sheet and spot a bad deal.
⚠️ Running a real agency, managing investors and surviving a scandal are beyond you.
⚖️ No accounting certification and no capital, and only a licensed hero can found a hero agency.
🏫 It shows in practical questions about cost, revenue and who pays.

📈 Grants: Business +15
Studied: Business.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has studied business: budgets, accounting, marketing, staffing, contracts, brand strategy and how a hero agency or a company makes money. They can read a balance sheet and spot a bad deal. Prior study, not mastery: running a real agency, managing investors and surviving a scandal are beyond them. Not a license: it is no accounting certification and no capital, and only a licensed hero can found a hero agency. It shows in practical questions about cost, revenue and who pays.

Studied: Psychology.name: Studied: Psychology
Studied: Psychology.description:
💭 You studied the mind: psychology courses, a peer counseling program or volunteer shifts on a support line.

🌱 Stress and trauma responses, motivation, group behavior and basic counseling. You recognize panic, shock and grief and respond in ways that help.
⚠️ Deep trauma, serious mental illness and skilled manipulators are beyond you.
⚖️ You are not a counselor or clinician: you cannot diagnose or treat, and you refer people to professionals.
🏫 It shows in patient questions, careful wording and a habit of noticing who has gone quiet.

📈 Grants: Psychology +15
Studied: Psychology.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has studied psychology: development, stress and trauma responses, motivation, group behavior and the basics of counseling and profiling. They recognize panic, shock and grief and respond in ways that help. Prior study, not mastery: deep trauma, serious mental illness and skilled manipulators are beyond them. Not a license: they are not a counselor or clinician, cannot diagnose or treat, and refer people to professionals. It shows in patient questions, careful wording and a habit of noticing who has gone quiet.

Studied: Languages.name: Studied: Languages
Studied: Languages.description:
🌏 You studied foreign languages: extra English classes, a year abroad, a family that spoke another language or translation work.

🌱 You speak at least one foreign language at a working level, English unless your background says otherwise, and know its culture's basics.
⚠️ Slang, regional accents, technical vocabulary and fast speech still trip you.
⚖️ It is no interpreter's certification.
🏫 It shows in a dictionary app, borrowed phrases and confidence when a foreign visitor needs help.

📈 Grants: Languages +15
Studied: Languages.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has studied at least one foreign language to a working level, English unless their background says otherwise. They can hold conversations, read documents and help visitors from overseas, and they know enough of the culture to avoid obvious mistakes. Prior study, not mastery: slang, regional accents, technical vocabulary and fast speech still trip them. Not a license: it is no interpreter's certification. It shows in a dictionary app, borrowed phrases and confidence when a foreign visitor needs help.

Studied: Support Engineering.name: Studied: Support Engineering
Studied: Support Engineering.description:
⚙️ You studied support design: an engineering program, a technical high school or nights spent rebuilding broken gear.

🌱 How support items are designed, tested and fitted to a Quirk. You can diagnose a fault and suggest gear that covers a Quirk's weakness.
⚠️ New inventions, high-power systems and miniaturized parts still fail more often than they work.
⚖️ Hero gear needs approval from a school, an agency or a licensed support company, and building gear for criminals is a crime.
🏫 It shows in notebooks of sketches and a habit of taking things apart.

📈 Grants: Support Engineering +15
Studied: Support Engineering.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has studied support engineering: how support items and costume systems are designed, tested and fitted to a Quirk, from frames and power supplies to safety cutoffs. They can diagnose a fault, sketch a design and suggest gear that covers a Quirk's weakness. Prior study, not mastery: new inventions, high-power systems and miniaturized parts still fail more often than they work. Not a license: gear for hero work needs approval from a school, an agency or a licensed support company, and building gear for criminals is a crime. It shows in notebooks of sketches and a habit of taking things apart.

Studied: Fabrication.name: Studied: Fabrication
Studied: Fabrication.description:
🛠️ You learned to make things by hand: a technical school, a machine shop job, welding classes or a family workshop.

🌱 Machining, welding, soldering, wiring and reading plans. You can repair a broken support item when the parts exist.
⚠️ Precision parts, unusual materials and complex electronics still need better tools and time.
⚖️ Making weapons or illegal gear is a crime, and workshop rules decide who runs the heavy machines.
🏫 It shows in small burn marks, steady hands and pockets full of tools.

📈 Grants: Fabrication +15
Studied: Fabrication.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has trained in hands-on making: machining, welding, soldering, wiring, sewing heavy materials, reading plans and assembling parts that fit. They can repair a broken support item when the parts exist. Prior study, not mastery: precision parts, unusual materials and complex electronics still need better tools and time. Not a license: making weapons or illegal gear is a crime, and workshop rules decide who may run the heavy machines. It shows in small burn marks, steady hands and pockets full of tools.

Studied: Computing.name: Studied: Computing
Studied: Computing.description:
💻 You studied computers: programming classes, a networking certificate, hobby projects or an IT part-time job.

🌱 You can write a script, recover deleted files and lock down a device, and you know the basics of intrusion.
⚠️ Hardened systems, government databases and a skilled defender are beyond you.
⚖️ Unauthorized access to any system is a crime, and police trace intrusions.
🏫 It shows in a sticker-covered laptop, many open windows and a reflex to check a device's security.

📈 Grants: Computing +15
Studied: Computing.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has studied computing: programming, networks, data recovery, security systems and the basics of intrusion. They can write a script, recover deleted files and lock down a device. Prior study, not mastery: hardened systems, government databases and a skilled defender are beyond them. Not a license: unauthorized access to any system is a crime, and police trace intrusions. It shows in a laptop covered in stickers, several windows open at once and a reflex to check a device's security.

Studied: Driving.name: Studied: Driving
Studied: Driving.description:
🚗 You went through driving school and drive well: cars, vans and city traffic.

🌱 You hold an ordinary license for cars and small vans and drive with control in traffic, in rain and on narrow streets.
⚠️ High-speed pursuit, evasive driving and heavy trucks are beyond you.
⚖️ No motorcycle, large-vehicle or emergency-vehicle license unless your background says so, and no exemption from traffic law in a chase.
🏫 It shows in easy confidence behind the wheel and eyes that check the mirrors.

📈 Grants: Driving +15
Studied: Driving.traitNarrativeEffects: The character finished driving school and holds an ordinary driver's license for cars and small vans. They drive with control in traffic, in rain and on narrow streets, and know the basics of keeping a vehicle running. Prior study, not mastery: high-speed pursuit, evasive driving and heavy trucks are beyond them. Not a license beyond that one: no motorcycle, large-vehicle or emergency-vehicle license unless their background says so, and no exemption from traffic law in a chase. It shows in easy confidence behind the wheel and eyes that check the mirrors.

Studied: Costume Design.name: Studied: Costume Design
Studied: Costume Design.description:
🧵 You studied fashion and costume design: a design school course, cosplay workshops or sewing for a theater company.

🌱 Materials, fit, movement and silhouette, adapted to a Quirk's heat, size changes or extra limbs. You can write a clear request for a support company.
⚠️ Armored or powered costumes and fabrics that survive extreme Quirks need support engineers.
⚖️ Designing a hero costume gives no right to wear one in public, and copying a pro's look invites trouble with their agency.
🏫 It shows in sketches, fabric swatches and opinions about everyone's outfit.

📈 Grants: Costume Design +15
Studied: Costume Design.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has studied costume design: materials, fit, movement, color and silhouette, durability and adapting an outfit to a Quirk's heat, size changes or extra limbs. They can write a clear design request for a support company and sketch alternatives. Prior study, not mastery: armored or powered costumes and fabrics that survive extreme Quirks need support engineers. Not a license: designing a hero costume gives no right to wear one as a hero in public, and copying a pro's look invites trouble with the agency that owns it. It shows in sketches, fabric swatches and opinions about everyone's outfit.

Studied: Media Production.name: Studied: Media Production
Studied: Media Production.description:
🎥 You learned to make media: a film club, photography courses, a video editing job or a streaming channel of your own.

🌱 Camera work, lighting, sound and editing. You can catch a fight or a rescue in a clear shot and turn it into something people watch.
⚠️ Live broadcasts under pressure and professional newsroom standards still challenge you.
⚖️ Filming gives no right to cross a police line, careless posting of faces brings complaints, and footage can be taken as evidence.
🏫 It shows in a camera always within reach and a habit of judging light and angles.

📈 Grants: Media Production +15
Studied: Media Production.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has studied media production: camera work, framing, lighting, sound, editing and publishing, from a short clip to a full report. They can catch a fight or a rescue in a clear shot and turn it into something people watch. Prior study, not mastery: live broadcasts under pressure and professional newsroom standards still challenge them. Not a license: filming gives no right to cross a police line or follow heroes into danger, publishing faces without care brings complaints, and footage can be taken as evidence. It shows in a camera always within reach and a habit of judging light and angles.

Studied: Performance.name: Studied: Performance
Studied: Performance.description:
🎤 You trained to perform: music lessons, a dance studio, a theater troupe, idol training or street performing.

🌱 Voice or instrument, dance, acting and stagecraft, with stage nerves under control. You can hold an audience and read its mood.
⚠️ A professional stage, a hostile crowd or performing while hurt still test you.
⚖️ Street performance may need a permit, and a Quirk used in a show follows the same public-use law as any other use.
🏫 It shows in rhythm, posture and a habit of humming or rehearsing under your breath.

📈 Grants: Performance +15
Studied: Performance.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has trained as a performer: an instrument or voice, dance, acting or stagecraft, with rehearsal discipline and stage nerves under control. They can hold an audience and read its mood. Prior study, not mastery: a professional stage, a hostile crowd or performing while hurt still test them. Not a license: street performance may need a permit, and a Quirk used in a show follows the same public-use law as any other use. It shows in rhythm, posture and a habit of humming or rehearsing under their breath.

Studied: Cooking.name: Studied: Cooking
Studied: Cooking.description:
🍳 You learned to cook properly: a family restaurant kitchen, culinary school classes or years of feeding younger siblings.

🌱 Knife work, rice and stock, frying, baking and food safety. You can feed a dorm floor or hold a station in a restaurant kitchen.
⚠️ Fine dining, specialist cuisines and running a whole kitchen are beyond you.
⚖️ Selling food needs a food hygiene permit.
🏫 It shows in clean knife cuts, a tidy kitchen and a habit of feeding people who look tired.

📈 Grants: Cooking +15
Studied: Cooking.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has trained in cooking: knife work, rice and stock, frying, baking, food safety, feeding a crowd on a budget and meals for bodies in hard training. They can feed a dorm floor or hold a station in a restaurant kitchen. Prior study, not mastery: fine dining, specialist cuisines and running a whole kitchen are beyond them. Not a license: selling food needs a food hygiene permit. It shows in clean knife cuts, a tidy kitchen and a habit of feeding people who look tired.

Studied: Survival.name: Studied: Survival
Studied: Survival.description:
🏕️ You learned to live outdoors: a mountain club, scouting, a rural childhood or disaster preparedness training.

🌱 Shelter, fire, water, foraging and weather signs. You know what to pack for an earthquake or a night on a mountain.
⚠️ Winter mountains, injuries far from help and long stretches without supplies still threaten you.
⚖️ Hunting, fishing and camping often need permits, and survival skills give no right to enter closed land or a disaster zone.
🏫 It shows in a packed emergency bag, a habit of checking the sky and calm during a blackout.

📈 Grants: Survival +15
Studied: Survival.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has trained in outdoor survival: shelter, fire, water, foraging, weather signs and keeping calm when lost. They know what to pack for an earthquake or a night on a mountain. Prior study, not mastery: winter mountains, injuries far from help and long stretches without supplies still threaten them. Not a license: hunting, fishing and camping often need permits, and survival skills give no right to enter closed land or a disaster zone. It shows in a packed emergency bag, a habit of checking the sky and calm during a blackout.

Rescue Kit.name: Rescue Kit
Rescue Kit.description:
⛑️ You carry a bag packed for accidents and disasters.

⚖️ All of it is legal to own and carry anywhere.
🤝 People who see it take you for someone who expects to help.
⚠️ Rescue gear gives no authority at a disaster: heroes, firefighters and police control the scene, and crossing a cordon is an offense.
🔄 Used supplies run out and are restocked at a pharmacy or a hero supply store.

🎒 Starts with: First aid kit ×3, Respirator mask, Climbing rope, Flashlight
Rescue Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: The character owns a rescue bag: a stocked first aid kit, a filter mask against smoke, dust and gas, a coil of rescue-rated rope and a bright waterproof flashlight. All of it is legal to own and carry anywhere, and people who see it take the character for someone who expects to help. Owning rescue gear gives no authority at a disaster: heroes, firefighters and police control the scene, and crossing a cordon is still an offense. Used supplies run out and are restocked at a pharmacy or a hero supply store.

Support Starter Kit.name: Support Starter Kit
Support Starter Kit.description:
🥽 You own entry-level support gear from a licensed support company.

⚖️ All of it is sold to the public and legal to own and wear.
⚠️ Gear is not a license: wearing it while chasing criminals is still vigilantism.
🏫 School exercises, exams and events can ban gear that was not approved in advance.
🔧 It only helps while worn, it can break, and repairs go through a support workshop.

🎒 Starts with: Support goggles, Grip gloves, Comms earpiece
Support Starter Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: The character owns entry-level support gear: tinted goggles with zoom and glare filtering, high-friction gloves and an encrypted earpiece paired to a channel they share with friends, teammates or classmates. All of it is sold to the public and legal to own and wear. Gear is not a license: wearing it while chasing criminals is still vigilantism, and school exercises, exams and events can ban gear that was not approved in advance. It only helps while worn, it can break, and repairs go through a support workshop.

Street Kit.name: Street Kit
Street Kit.description:
🌃 You carry what someone who walks the city at night carries.

🎯 The kit of a night patroller, a would-be vigilante or someone who expects trouble on the way home.
⚖️ The mask, ties and flashlight are legal. Carrying the baton without good reason is illegal, and police who find it can confiscate it and charge you.
⚠️ A baton and a mask together near a crime read as vigilante or villain intent.
🪢 Tying someone up is legal only to hold a person caught in the act until the police arrive.

🎒 Starts with: Domino mask, Telescoping baton, Zip ties ×5, Flashlight
Street Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: The character carries a simple eye mask, a collapsible steel baton, a bundle of heavy zip ties and a flashlight: the kit of a night patroller, a would-be vigilante or someone who expects trouble on the way home. The mask, ties and flashlight are legal. Carrying the baton without a legitimate reason is illegal: police who search the character confiscate it and can charge them, and a baton and a mask together near a crime read as vigilante or villain intent. Tying someone up is legal only when holding a person caught in the act until the police arrive.

Villain Kit.name: Villain Kit
Villain Kit.description:
🦹 You own black-market tools for crime.

⚖️ Carrying this kit is illegal: the knife, the lockpicks and the smoke grenades all break the law in public.
🚨 A police stop that finds it means confiscation, arrest and a record, and heroes treat you as a villain from then on.
🤝 The broker who sold it knows your face.
🔄 Smoke grenades are spent on use and can only be replaced through the underworld.

🎒 Starts with: Balaclava, Combat knife, Lockpick set, Smoke grenade ×2
Villain Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: The character owns a criminal's working kit bought through a black-market broker: a knit face covering, a fixed-blade knife, picks with tension wrenches and a bump key, and two smoke canisters. Carrying it is illegal: the knife breaks weapons law in public, lockpicks without a trade reason are banned, and smoke grenades are restricted to heroes and police. A police stop that finds the kit means confiscation, arrest and a record, and heroes treat the carrier as a villain from that moment. The broker who sold it knows the character's face. Smoke grenades are spent on use and can only be replaced through the underworld.

Study Kit.name: Study Kit
Study Kit.description:
✏️ You carry a student's desk in a bag.

⚖️ All of it is legal and ordinary.
📖 The textbooks match your course, or whatever you last studied.
⚠️ Your Quirk notebook is private: if lost, it can embarrass you and help a villain.
☕ The coffee is gone once drunk.

🎒 Starts with: Course textbooks, Quirk analysis notebook, Omamori charm, Canned coffee ×3
Study Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: The character owns the term's textbooks and lecture notes, a notebook for recording and sketching the Quirks they observe, a shrine charm bought for success in exams and a few cans of vending-machine coffee. All of it is legal and ordinary. For a student the textbooks match their course; for anyone else they are the books of whatever they last studied. The notebook is private and sensitive: notes on other people's Quirks can embarrass the writer and help a villain if it is lost. The coffee is gone once drunk.

Athlete Kit.name: Athlete Kit
Athlete Kit.description:
👟 You carry gear for a body in daily training.

⚖️ All of it is legal to own; the boots are a commercial support item sold to the public.
🏫 School competitions can ban support items for students outside the Support Course, so the boots may stay in a locker on event days.
🔄 Protein bars and ice packs are used up on use.

🎒 Starts with: Fitness tracker, Support boots, Protein bar ×4, Ice pack ×2
Athlete Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: The character owns a wristband that tracks heart rate and training, spring-soled support boots with ankle support and grip, a stash of protein bars and instant cold packs for sprains and bruises. All of it is legal; the boots are a commercial support item sold to the public. School competitions can ban support items for students outside the Support Course, so the boots may stay in a locker on event days. Bars and cold packs are used up on use.

Tech Kit.name: Tech Kit
Tech Kit.description:
🔌 You carry tools for building, fixing and coding.

⚖️ All of it is legal to own, but breaking into systems with the laptop is a crime.
⚠️ Modifying someone's support gear without permission can void its approval and make you answerable for any failure.
🔄 Spare parts run low with heavy use and are restocked at electronics shops or a support workshop.

🎒 Starts with: Laptop, Support toolkit, Energy drink ×3
Tech Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: The character owns a portable computer set up for coding and design, a support toolkit with drivers, a multimeter, a soldering iron and spare parts, and a few cans of energy drink for late nights. All of it is legal. Breaking into systems with the laptop is a crime, and modifying someone's support gear without permission can void its approval and make the character answerable for any failure. Spare parts run low with heavy use and are restocked at electronics shops or a support workshop.

Everyday Kit.name: Everyday Kit
Everyday Kit.description:
🍙 You carry ordinary comforts for daily life.

⚖️ All of it is legal and unremarkable.
👕 Casual clothes let you leave a uniform or costume behind and blend into a crowd.
🔄 Food and medicine are used up on use and restocked at any convenience store or pharmacy.

🎒 Starts with: Casual clothes, Bento box ×2, Painkillers, Bandages ×2, Omamori charm
Everyday Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has a set of everyday clothes for off-duty hours, boxed lunches, over-the-counter pain tablets, some bandage and tape, and a shrine charm for safety tied to their bag. All of it is legal and unremarkable. Casual clothes let them leave a uniform or costume behind and blend into a crowd, which matters to anyone who wants a private life apart from school, work or a hero identity. Food and medicine are used up on use and restocked at any convenience store or pharmacy.

Media Kit.name: Media Kit
Media Kit.description:
📷 You carry gear for making and sharing content.

⚖️ All of it is legal to own, and filming in public is allowed.
⚠️ Crossing a police or hero cordon for a shot is obstruction, posting private faces brings complaints, and footage can be demanded as evidence.
🤝 Handing out cards makes you easy to find for fans, sponsors and anyone with a grudge.

🎒 Starts with: Camera, Tablet, Business cards
Media Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: The character owns a camera for photos and video, a tablet for editing, notes and presentations, and a box of business cards with their name and contact details or channel. All of it is legal. Filming in public is allowed, but crossing a police or hero cordon for a shot is obstruction, posting private faces brings complaints, and footage of a crime can be demanded as evidence. Handing out cards makes the character easy to find for fans, sponsors and anyone with a grudge.

No Gear Set.name: No Gear Set
No Gear Set.description:
📱 You start with only what everyone has: a smartphone, an IC transit card and some cash.

🌱 You also get whatever your Path and other traits give.
🛒 Anything else you need, you buy, borrow, are issued or earn in play.
No Gear Set.traitNarrativeEffects: The character starts with no extra gear: only the smartphone, transit card and cash everyone has, plus whatever their Path and other traits grant. Do not invent extra equipment for them at the start. Anything else they need, they buy, borrow, are issued or earn in play.

Quirk Breakthrough.name: Quirk Breakthrough
Quirk Breakthrough.description:
🚀 Your Quirk has broken through to a new level: more power, and the control to hold it.

🔓 It unlocks your Quirk's Ultimate technique, which still needs the matching Quirk skill at 45 to learn.
📋 As a level-up pick it requires level 8 and Quirk Control 15. The story can also grant it at a turning point.
➡️ It opens the way to Quirk Awakening at level 24.
🚫 Not available to Quirkless characters.

📈 Grants: Quirk Control +5, Quirk Output +5
Quirk Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's Quirk has broken through to a new level. Mark the moment with a scene in which the Quirk does something it never managed before: a longer reach, a heavier blow, a sharper shape or a cleaner stop. From then on the new level is steady and reliable. It unlocks Ultimate techniques: with enough skill, the user can now learn and use their signature move. Limits: the Quirk keeps its nature and family, it gains no new kind of power, the Drawback stays, and Ultimate techniques still cost severe Strain. Teachers, rivals, agencies and villains notice the jump, and the character's registered Quirk details may need updating. If the character chose Quirkless, this trait does not apply: they have no Quirk to break through.

Quirk Endurance.name: Quirk Endurance
Quirk Endurance.description:
🔋 Repeated use has taught your body to keep its Quirk running and to push through the drawback when it bites.

📋 Requires level 8 and Quirk Stamina 8.
🚫 Not available to Quirkless characters.

📈 Grants: Quirk Stamina +10
Quirk Endurance.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has pushed their Quirk past its early limits through repetition: long sessions, back-to-back uses and practice at high Strain. Show it as composure while the Quirk runs: steadier breathing, fewer tremors and less visible distress as Strain climbs. They know their body's warning signs and work through the first ones safely. Limits: Strain still rises at the same rate and the Drawback still shows at its thresholds; this is endurance, not immunity, and a severe technique costs what it always cost. If the character chose Quirkless, this trait does not apply.

Battle Instinct.name: Battle Instinct
Battle Instinct.description:
⚔️ Fights have taught you to move before you finish thinking.

👁️ You see the opening and the incoming blow a moment sooner.
📋 Requires level 8 and Combat Tactics 10.

📈 Grants: Dodging +5, Combat Tactics +5
Battle Instinct.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has fought enough to read a fight's rhythm by instinct: they shift away from a blow as it starts, notice when an opponent overcommits and keep track of everyone in view. Show it in quick, economical reactions and a calm sense of timing. Limits: it works on what they can perceive; an unseen attacker, a hidden Quirk or an ambush from outside their senses still catches them. It is experience, not foresight or a Quirk.

Rescue Instinct.name: Rescue Instinct
Rescue Instinct.description:
🚑 You see the people in danger first.

👁️ You spot who is trapped, who is bleeding and who needs to move now.
📋 Requires level 8 and Search and Rescue 10.

📈 Grants: Search and Rescue +5, First Aid +5
Rescue Instinct.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's priorities in a crisis have become automatic: on arrival they find the people in danger, spot the trapped and the injured and pick the fastest safe way to reach them before thinking about the fight. Show it in quick triage, steady hands under rubble and calm words to victims. Limits: instinct does not lift a collapsed floor or replace a surgeon; it chooses well, it does not do the impossible. It also pulls them toward victims while the villain is still standing.

Crowd Reader.name: Crowd Reader
Crowd Reader.description:
👥 You can feel a crowd's mood and steer it.

👁️ You see who is about to panic, who will help and where people will run.
📋 Requires level 8 and Cooperativeness 12.

📈 Grants: Insight +5, Evacuation +5
Crowd Reader.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has learned to read groups of people: the shift in mood before a crowd panics, the bystander about to film instead of flee, the person who will help if asked by name. Show it as quick, targeted words and gestures that move people the right way. Limits: it works on ordinary people in ordinary fear; a mind-affecting Quirk, a riot already in motion or a crowd that cannot hear them is beyond it. It reads behavior, not thoughts.

Steady Nerves.name: Steady Nerves
Steady Nerves.description:
🧘 Fear still comes, but it no longer decides for you.

🎯 Good for keeping your head when things go wrong.
📋 Requires level 8 and Willpower 8.

📈 Grants: Willpower +10
Steady Nerves.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has faced enough danger to keep their head: they feel fear and act anyway. Show steady breathing, clear decisions under threat and a refusal to be rushed by intimidation or a killer's stare. Limits: they are brave, not fearless; trauma still leaves marks, and strong mind-affecting Quirks can still take hold, though the character fights them harder.

Street Smarts.name: Street Smarts
Street Smarts.description:
🌃 You know how the city's underside works.

🧭 You know who sells what, which streets belong to whom and when to walk away.
📋 Requires level 8 and Streetwise 8.

📈 Grants: Streetwise +10
Street Smarts.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has spent enough time in the city's rough corners to read them: they spot gang territory, recognize a broker's front business, pick up useful rumors in back-alley bars and arcades and notice when a deal is a trap. Show it as quiet caution and the right question to the right person. Limits: knowing the street is not being trusted by it; the underworld still lies, and organized villains keep their secrets from small-time contacts. Heroes and police may read this familiarity as a sign of criminal ties.

Field Analyst.name: Field Analyst
Field Analyst.description:
🔍 You read Quirks fast: what one does, where its limit is and how to beat it.

🎯 Good for planners and anyone who faces stronger Quirks. Quirkless characters can take it too.
📋 Requires level 8 and Quirk Analysis 10.

📈 Grants: Quirk Analysis +10
Field Analyst.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has watched, logged and faced enough Quirks to analyze them on the move: from a few uses they work out a Quirk's type, range, trigger and likely weakness, and they adjust the plan as evidence comes in. Show it in sharp observations shared with allies and notes after a fight. Limits: conclusions can be wrong; hidden activation conditions, deliberate deception and Quirks never seen before still surprise them. Analysis gives answers, not the power to act on them.

In Sync.name: In Sync
In Sync.description:
🤝 You fight and work in step with others.

🫱 You cover a partner, time your move to theirs and combine efforts without a word.
📋 Requires level 8 and Team Coordination 8.

📈 Grants: Team Coordination +10
In Sync.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has trained and fought beside others long enough to move in step: they read a partner's intent from posture, cover blind spots, time attacks and rescues to combine with an ally's Quirk and pass on information without being asked. Show it in wordless combinations and smooth handoffs. Limits: it works best with people they have practiced with; a stranger or a teammate who refuses to cooperate gives them little to work with.

Deep Reserves.name: Deep Reserves
Deep Reserves.description:
🏃 Hard daily training has built your stamina.

🔋 You outlast fights, climbs and rescues that wear others out.
📋 Requires level 8 and Conditioning 8.

📈 Grants: Stamina +15
Deep Reserves.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's body has adapted to hard daily training: stronger lungs and legs and faster recovery between efforts. Show it in steady breathing late in a fight and energy to spare after drills. Limits: it adds staying power, not strength or speed, and lost sleep, injury and hunger still drain them.

Pinpoint Control.name: Pinpoint Control
Pinpoint Control.description:
🎯 You place your Quirk exactly where you mean it.

✨ A narrow strike past a hostage, a gentle touch, a partial use on demand.
📋 Requires level 16 and Quirk Control 22.
🚫 Not available to Quirkless characters.

📈 Grants: Quirk Control +10
Pinpoint Control.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has refined fine control of their Quirk: they can shrink its area, dial its force down to what the moment needs, aim it past an ally or a hostage and stop it the instant they decide. Show precision in small details: an effect that ends exactly at a line, a strike that bruises instead of breaking bone, a use so measured it looks easy. Limits: precision adds no range or power, and fatigue, panic and high Strain still loosen control. If the character chose Quirkless, this trait does not apply.

Aerial Control.name: Aerial Control
Aerial Control.description:
🪂 You move through the air with control.

🌀 Tighter turns, cleaner landings and the balance to act or carry someone while airborne.
📋 Requires level 16 and Quirk Mobility 15.
🚫 Not available to Quirkless characters.

📈 Grants: Quirk Mobility +5, Acrobatics +5
Aerial Control.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has learned to control their body in the air while their Quirk moves them: they correct a spin, change direction mid-leap or mid-flight, land on a narrow ledge and keep their bearings in a fall. Show it in smooth arcs, sure landings and the confidence to act in midair. Limits: it improves handling, not the Quirk's range, speed or lift; a Quirk that cannot fly still cannot fly, and passengers, wind and high Strain still make air work dangerous. Moving through the city by Quirk is public Quirk use and needs a license or an emergency. If the character chose Quirkless, this trait does not apply.

Command Presence.name: Command Presence
Command Presence.description:
📣 People listen when you give an order in a crisis.

🎯 Good for team leaders, teachers and agency heads.
📋 Requires level 16 and Leadership 15.

📈 Grants: Leadership +10
Command Presence.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has led people through danger and it shows: their orders are short and clear, they assign tasks by people's strengths and they take responsibility when it goes wrong. In a crisis, classmates, sidekicks, bystanders or gang members turn to them for direction. Show it in decisive calls and a voice that carries. Limits: authority still comes from rank and law; a pro at the scene, a teacher or a superior in their organization outranks them, and people follow bad orders less willingly each time.

Hold the Line.name: Hold the Line
Hold the Line.description:
🛡️ You can stand between a blow and the people behind you, and stay standing.

🎯 Good for defenders and anyone who shields civilians in a fight.
📋 Requires level 16 and Blocking 15.

📈 Grants: Blocking +10
Hold the Line.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has learned to take hits on purpose: they angle a guard, a shield, armor or their own toughened limbs to turn an impact, brace their stance and keep their feet to protect someone behind them. Show it in a planted stance and a refusal to give ground. Limits: it reduces and redirects impacts rather than stopping all harm; a strong enough blow still injures, and blocking blades, acid or flame with bare arms still costs them.

Pain Tolerance.name: Pain Tolerance
Pain Tolerance.description:
🩹 You keep functioning through injuries that would drop most people.

⚠️ It heals nothing: injuries you ignore still get worse.
📋 Requires level 16 and Conditioning 15.

📈 Grants: Health +15
Pain Tolerance.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has been hurt often enough to work through pain: they stay conscious, keep moving and think clearly through bruises, burns and cracked ribs. Show it as grim focus and injuries noticed only after the fight. Limits: tolerance heals nothing; ignored injuries get worse, Recovery Girl or a hospital doctor will still order rest, and a hard blow to the head still knocks them out.

Media Savvy.name: Media Savvy
Media Savvy.description:
📸 You handle cameras, reporters and fans with ease, and turn attention to your advantage.

🎯 Good for pros chasing the rankings and anyone in the public eye.
📋 Requires level 16 and Media Presence 18.

📈 Grants: Media Presence +10
Media Savvy.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has been in public view enough to handle it: they give clean answers to reporters, sense a loaded question, choose what to post and turn a viral moment to their advantage. Show it in composed interviews and a public image that survives small mistakes. Limits: savvy cannot erase a real scandal, and attention draws enemies: villains, rivals and journalists digging for the story behind the image.

Heavy Hitter.name: Heavy Hitter
Heavy Hitter.description:
👊 Your strikes, lifts and blows carry more force.

🎯 Good for fighters who win up close.
📋 Requires level 16 and Power 13.

📈 Grants: Power +1
Heavy Hitter.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's strength has grown through training and fights: they hit harder, lift more and drive force through their whole stance. Show it in dented targets, opponents staggered by a single blow and doors that give way. Limits: more force means more danger to the people they hit; holding back takes conscious effort, and excessive force is a legal problem for heroes and civilians alike.

Quick Reflexes.name: Quick Reflexes
Quick Reflexes.description:
⚡ You react faster: a step ahead on the draw, the dodge and the sprint.

🎯 Good for anyone who needs to move first.
📋 Requires level 16 and Speed 13.

📈 Grants: Speed +1
Quick Reflexes.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's reaction speed has sharpened: they move first when a fight starts, catch falling objects and clear the space before a blow lands. Show it in quick hands and fast first steps. Limits: it is human reflex refined by training, not a speed Quirk; it gives no extra actions and still loses to an attack they cannot see coming.

Clean Technique.name: Clean Technique
Clean Technique.description:
🖐️ Your movements are precise and practiced: cleaner strikes, steadier hands, finer work.

🎯 Good for martial artists, builders and anyone who works with fine control.
📋 Requires level 16 and Technique 13.

📈 Grants: Technique +1
Clean Technique.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has refined their form through repetition: blows land where they aim, tools do what they intend, holds lock on the first attempt and fine work comes out right. Show it in efficient, unhurried motions with nothing wasted. Limits: precision adds no strength, and exhaustion and fear still shake the hands.

Raw Output.name: Raw Output
Raw Output.description:
🔥 Your Quirk hits harder than it did: more force, more area, more heat or charge behind every use.

📋 Requires level 24 and Quirk Output 28.
🚫 Not available to Quirkless characters.

📈 Grants: Quirk Output +10
Raw Output.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's Quirk has grown in raw force through training and use: blasts land harder, effects cover more ground and obstacles that once stopped them now give way. Show it in the aftermath: deeper craters, louder impacts and opponents who start taking them seriously. Limits: more power means more danger near bystanders and makes holding back harder; Strain costs do not change, and the Quirk keeps its nature and its Drawback. Police and pros judge any injury it causes by the force the character chose to use. If the character chose Quirkless, this trait does not apply.

Sharp Mind.name: Sharp Mind
Sharp Mind.description:
💭 Experience has made you quicker to connect facts and plan ahead.

🎯 Good for strategists and planners.
📋 Requires level 24 and Intelligence 14.

📈 Grants: Intelligence +1
Sharp Mind.traitNarrativeEffects: The character thinks faster and more clearly than when they started: they connect facts across cases, remember details and plan several steps ahead. Show it in quick deductions and plans that anticipate problems. Limits: intelligence is not knowledge; they still need to learn facts, and they still misjudge people.

Trusted Partner.name: Trusted Partner
Trusted Partner.description:
🫂 People rely on you and open up to you: allies, victims and strangers alike.

🎯 Good for anyone who wins people over or holds a team together.
📋 Requires level 24 and Cooperativeness 14.

📈 Grants: Cooperativeness +1
Trusted Partner.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has a record of keeping their word and showing up, and people sense it: allies share plans, victims accept help and strangers answer questions. Show it in easy rapport and people who seek them out. Limits: trust is earned person by person; enemies, the prejudiced and anyone they have betrayed are not won over by this.

Iron Constitution.name: Iron Constitution
Iron Constitution.description:
🪨 Your body has toughened: you shake off illness, cold and exhaustion and take a hit better.

🎯 Good for front-liners and anyone who works long, hard shifts.
📋 Requires level 24 and Endurance 14.

📈 Grants: Endurance +1
Iron Constitution.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's body has toughened through a long stretch of training, injury and recovery: they recover from illness quickly, handle heat and cold and absorb blows that would stagger others. Show it in a solid frame and quick recovery. Limits: it toughens the body, not the mind, and it does not resist Quirk effects that bypass the body.

Provisional Hero License.name: Provisional Hero License
Provisional Hero License.description:
🔰 You passed the Hero Public Safety Commission's provisional license exam.

⚖️ You may use your Quirk in emergencies and do hero work under a licensed hero.
⚠️ No patrolling or villain hunting on your own, no sidekick work and no agency of your own.
🤝 Police and the public treat you as a hero in training: trusted to help, expected to defer to the pros.

📈 Grants: Hero Law +5
🎒 Starts with: Provisional hero license
Provisional Hero License.traitNarrativeEffects: A provisional hero license, issued by the Hero Public Safety Commission after its licensing exam. It permits: using their Quirk to protect people and stop an immediate threat in an emergency without waiting for supervision; hero work studies and internships at an agency under a licensed pro; joining hero operations when a licensed hero or the police direct them. It forbids: patrolling or hunting villains on their own initiative, running their own operations, sidekick work, opening an agency, and any public Quirk use outside an emergency or supervised work. Their use of force is judged by a pro's standard. Misuse is reported to their school or supervising agency, and the Commission can suspend or revoke the license. Police and the public treat them as heroes in training: trusted to help, expected to defer to the pros. A Quirkless holder follows the same rules with gear and training in place of a Quirk. If they also hold Hero License, the full license governs.

Hero License.name: Hero License
Hero License.description:
🪪 You are a licensed professional hero, certified by the Hero Public Safety Commission.

⚖️ You may use your Quirk in hero work, patrol, apprehend villains, and work for or found an agency.
⚠️ You report every incident and answer for any damage you cause. Misconduct can cost you the license.
🤝 You are a public figure: rankings, press, fans, sponsors and villains all watch you.
🔁 It replaces a Provisional Hero License if you hold one.

📈 Grants: Hero Law +5
🎒 Starts with: Hero license
Hero License.traitNarrativeEffects: Holds a full hero license from the Hero Public Safety Commission; it replaces a Provisional Hero License if held. Rights: Quirk use in public in the course of hero work; patrols; responding to crimes, accidents and disasters; apprehending villains and handing them to police; reasonable force; working as a sidekick, joining or founding an agency and hiring sidekicks; pay from agency contracts, government compensation and endorsements; a place on the Hero Billboard Chart JP, the official pro hero ranking. Duties: report every incident and Quirk use; respect police authority over investigations and crime scenes; use only the force needed; answer for injuries and property damage caused; answer Commission calls in a large crisis. Misconduct brings suspension or revocation and can bring criminal charges. A public figure: rankings, press, fans, sponsors and villains watch. A Quirkless holder works under the same rules with gear and training in place of a Quirk.

Fire Quirk.name: Fire Quirk
Fire Quirk.description:
🔥 You make real fire from your body.

🌱 At the start you throw flame jets and bursts out to about five meters, raise a fire screen between you and danger, and give light and heat on demand.
📈 With training: flame lances, signal flares, thrust leaps, fire lanes that stop a spreading blaze, steel-melting white heat, and flame shaped to spare a hostage.
⚠️ Holding back is the real skill: every burn you cause is yours to answer for.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Overheating, as heat builds inside your own body.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Endeavor (Hellflame), Dabi (Cremation).

📈 Grants: Power +1, Quirk Output +10, Quirk Control +10, Conditioning +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Ember Jet, Blaze Screen
🛡️ Resists: fire
Fire Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: flame from the skin, usually palms and forearms. At first: a jet about five meters, a doorway-filling burst, flame a few seconds per push; it lights wood, cloth and fuel; dirty flame makes thick smoke. More needs learned techniques. Limits: water, foam, rain and sealed rooms smother it; fire spreads to what it touches, smoke chokes allies too, and clothes burn unless fireproof. The user resists heat, not smoke, and cannot call back a fire that has caught. Quirk Strain: light: hand flame, short jet; moderate: fire screen, lance, flare, thrust leap; heavy: clearing a fire lane, melting steel; severe: signature move, flame shaped around people. Type: Emitter (also fits Mutant). Law: unlicensed public flame is a crime, burning a person assault; even licensed heroes answer for every avoidable burn. Look: none at rest; flame in the player's chosen color rolls off hands and arms with heat shimmer; as Mutant, a permanent mark such as flame hair or ember-lit skin.

Ice Quirk.name: Ice Quirk
Ice Quirk.description:
❄️ You make ice and frost from your body.

🌱 At the start it spreads from your hands and feet along the ground out to about ten meters: a surge that slows a foe, a slick sheet across a room, a head-high wall.
📈 With training: restraints that hold without harm, bullet-stopping ice, slide ramps, shoring that holds up a collapse, armor-shattering frost, a frozen city block.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Overheating, which runs cold for an ice Quirk, so frost and numbness creep into your own limbs.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Shoto Todoroki (Half-Cold Half-Hot, cold side).

📈 Grants: Technique +1, Quirk Output +10, Quirk Control +10, Combat Tactics +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Rime Rush, Black Ice Spread
🛡️ Resists: cold
Ice Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the user makes ice from the skin and spreads it along touched surfaces, or breathes frost (player's choice). A new adult user glazes a room's floor, raises a head-high wall or sends a frozen line about ten meters along the ground in a second or two; made ice is ordinary ice. Bigger feats need techniques. Limits: heat melts it, heavy blows crack it, allies slip too; it grows from surfaces, so fliers and leapers are hard to catch; ice left on a person too long causes frostbite. Quirk Strain: light: frost, slick floor, ground surge; moderate: restraint, wall, ramp; heavy: shoring a structure, shattering armor; severe: signature move, freezing a whole scene. Type: Emitter (also fits Mutant). Law: freezing a person without a license is assault; whoever ices a road answers for the crashes. Look: cool skin; in use, frost climbs the arm from the working hand, ice grows in blue-white sheets; as Mutant, a permanent feature such as frosted hair or shoulder crystals.

Electricity Quirk.name: Electricity Quirk
Electricity Quirk.description:
⚡ Your body stores electricity and releases it.

🌱 At the start you discharge a crackling burst at everyone within arm's reach, lock a person's muscles with a touch, and run a phone or a dead car battery for a while.
📈 With training and conductive tricks: one-target bolts, building blackouts and takeovers, a restarted heart, a nerve-driven blur, lightning chained through a crowd.
⚠️ Aiming is the hard part: your early bursts hit friend and foe alike.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Cognitive Fade, as overuse scrambles your thinking.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Denki Kaminari (Electrification).

📈 Grants: Speed +1, Quirk Output +10, Quirk Control +10, Support Engineering +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Static Burst, Jolt Clasp
🛡️ Resists: electric
Electricity Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the body stores charge and releases it through the skin. A new adult user discharges a burst about arm's length around, drops an adult with a touch shock, runs a phone or car battery some minutes. Untrained discharges spread every way; a bolt hits a chosen target only along a conductor (wire, thrown coin). Bigger feats need techniques. Limits: rubber, insulation and grounding blunt it; water carries it to everyone in it; nearby electronics can fry by accident. Cannot fly, block blows or move metal. Quirk Strain: light: burst, touch shock; moderate: guided bolt, blackout, restarting a heart; heavy: nerve-driven sprint, chained lightning; severe: signature discharge, seizing a building's power. Type: Emitter. Law: shocking a person unlicensed is assault; cutting power to traffic lights or hospitals is endangering the public. Look: static in the hair at rest; in use, yellow-white arcs (or player's color) crawl on the skin, lights flicker, ozone smell.

Explosion Quirk.name: Explosion Quirk
Explosion Quirk.description:
💥 Your palms fire explosive blasts.

🌱 At the start each blast reaches a few meters, cracks concrete and throws an adult off their feet, and a blast aimed behind you hurls you clear of danger.
📈 With training: focused shots down a street, flashes that blind and deafen without injury, flight on chained blasts, wall-breaching rescues, barrages, a diving sky strike.
⚠️ It is loud and bright every time, so you cannot hide it.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Recoil, as every blast jolts your wrists and arms.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Katsuki Bakugo (Explosion).

📈 Grants: Power +1, Quirk Output +10, Quirk Mobility +10, Striking +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Detonation Palm, Rocket Hop
🛡️ Resists: explosive
Explosion Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the user detonates blasts from the palms (or soles, by player choice). A new adult user's blast reaches a few meters, cracks concrete and throws an adult off their feet; aimed behind or below, it hurls the user a few meters at a time. Bigger feats need techniques. Limits: each blast hits everything in its cone, so crowds, hostages and fuel are real risks; bound or covered palms cannot fire; every blast is deafening and bright, so no stealth. At the start it cannot hover in place or make a quiet blast. Quirk Strain: light: a blast or hop; moderate: focused shot, flash, blast flight; heavy: breach, barrage; severe: signature dive, weaving through a whole scene. Type: Emitter. Law: an unlicensed public blast brings property and injury charges at once; police treat an unlicensed user as armed. Look: in use, palms glow and crackle; each blast throws an orange flash and gray smoke with a bang heard blocks away.

Sound Quirk.name: Sound Quirk
Sound Quirk.description:
🔊 You produce sound and shape it.

🌱 At the start your voice (or claps and stomps) carries about a kilometer, a cone of sound staggers everyone in front of you, and echoes map a dark room.
📈 With training: a balance-scrambling hum, evacuation calls over disaster noise, rides on sound to rooftops, shattered glass and concrete, street sweeps, a silent building.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Bodily Toll, as your throat and ears pay for the noise.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Present Mic (Voice), Kyoka Jiro (Earphone Jack).

📈 Grants: Cooperativeness +1, Quirk Output +10, Quirk Analysis +10, Perception +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Bellow Wave, Echo Sounding
🛡️ Resists: sonic
Sound Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: sound from the throat or, if the player chooses, claps and stomps, amplified and aimed. At first: heard clearly about a kilometer away, a shout staggers people within a few meters, and echoes map a room or rubble pile in darkness or smoke. More needs learned techniques. Limits: sound spreads, so anyone in front, allies and civilians included, is hit unless the user aims well; ear protection and thick walls blunt it, water muffles it; it cannot cut, burn or grip, and every use is heard. Quirk Strain: light: amplifying, shout, echo map; moderate: disorienting hum, carrying call, sound-driven leap; heavy: shattering note, sweep of sound; severe: signature beam, silencing a building. Type: Emitter. Law: a blast that ruptures eardrums or shatters windows over a crowd is assault and property damage; licensed users aim away from bystanders. Look: a strong voice at rest; in use, air ahead ripples, dust and paper jump, glass hums, throat, hands or feet vibrate.

Light Quirk.name: Light Quirk
Light Quirk.description:
✨ You build light inside your body and release it as beams and flashes.

🌱 At the start you fire a thin beam that sears skin about twenty meters away, flare bright enough to dazzle a room, and light up a dark building.
📈 With training: beams nobody can dodge, decoy light doubles, beam-kick leaps, cutting lines that free the trapped and seal wounds, a guarding turn, a street-wide beam.
⚠️ A full beam to the eyes can blind for life.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Bodily Toll, as forcing light out cramps the muscles it leaves through.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Yuga Aoyama (Navel Laser).

📈 Grants: Technique +1, Quirk Output +10, Quirk Control +10, Performance +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Glint Ray, Halo Glare
🛡️ Resists: light
Light Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the user builds light in the body and releases it from palms, chest or a player-chosen spot. A new adult user fires a thin beam about twenty meters that sears skin, flashes to dazzle a room, or lights a warehouse until they stop. More needs techniques. Limits: a beam burns but never shoves; its kick pushes the user back a step; mirrors bounce it, smoke, fog and rain scatter it, opaque cover stops it; no corners without a mirror; every beam reveals where the user stands; tinted visors or shut eyes blunt the dazzle. Quirk Strain: light: short beam, glow; moderate: dazzling flash, precise long beam, light double, beam-kick leap; heavy: cutting line, turning guard beam; severe: signature beam, disarming a whole scene. Type: Emitter. Law: a beam to the eyes can blind for life, so aiming at a face is serious assault; unlicensed public use is a crime even if nobody is hurt. Look: in use, the spot glows white or the player's color; beams show in dust and smoke.

Wind Quirk.name: Wind Quirk
Wind Quirk.description:
🌪️ You make wind and drive it where you aim.

🌱 At the start your gusts knock an adult off their feet about ten meters away, an updraft lifts you a story high, and you clear the smoke from a room.
📈 With training: cutting air edges, wind walls that turn thrown objects aside, true flight carrying others, smoke-pulling drafts, cyclones, a whole crowd flown to safety.
⚠️ Wind feeds fires and throws debris, so check what lies behind your target.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Loss of Control, as strong wind stops going where you aim it.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Inasa Yoarashi (Whirlwind).

📈 Grants: Power +1, Quirk Output +10, Quirk Mobility +10, Search and Rescue +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Gust Shove, Updraft Bound
Wind Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the user makes moving air and throws it from the hands (or whole body, player's choice). A new adult user's gust knocks an adult off their feet about ten meters away; an updraft lifts the user a story high or slows a fall; a draft clears a room of smoke in seconds. Bigger feats need techniques. Limits: wind moves everything in its path, so debris, glass and bystanders go with the target; it fans flames and pushes smoke and gas downwind. Braced or heavy targets hold; a sealed room only churns. At the start it cannot cut, keep anyone aloft past a moment, or pin anyone. Quirk Strain: light: gust, updraft hop; moderate: cutting edge, wind wall, flight; heavy: pulling smoke from a building, cyclone; severe: signature storm, flying a crowd to safety. Type: Emitter. Law: unlicensed public gusts are a crime; the user answers for every sign, window and pedestrian their wind throws into traffic. Look: in use, hair and clothes whip, dust spirals, air roars.

Water Quirk.name: Water Quirk
Water Quirk.description:
💧 Your body makes water and pushes it out under pressure.

🌱 At the start a jet knocks an adult down at close range, your spray puts out a burning room, and you hold a ball of your own water in shape for a few seconds.
📈 With training: shells that stop blows and fire, hallway-sweeping waves, jets up a building, turned floodwater, slugs that hit through any guard, command of a whole flood.
⚠️ Water held over a face can drown a person, so restraint comes first.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Finite Fuel, as every liter you push out has to be drunk back in.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Backdraft (Water Hose).

📈 Grants: Endurance +1, Quirk Output +10, Quirk Control +10, Search and Rescue +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Hydrant Shot, Dousing Fan
Water Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the body makes clean water, released from the palms or a player-chosen spot. A new adult user fires a jet about ten meters that knocks an adult down up close, puts out a burning room within a minute, and holds a head-sized water ball a few seconds. Bigger feats need techniques. Limits: the water carries current (a soaked area is dangerous near live wires and electric Quirks), turns grease fires into fireballs and makes floors slick; cold or ice Quirks freeze it. Force drops fast past range; at the start it cannot cut or steer water the user did not make. Quirk Strain: light: jet, spray, held ball; moderate: water shell, sweeping wave, geyser ride; heavy: turning floodwater, water hammer; severe: signature wave, commanding a flood. Type: Emitter. Law: water held over a mouth and nose is attempted homicide however brief; flooding a street or building brings property charges. Look: cool, damp palms; in use, beads well up, then pour out in a roaring stream.

Gravity Quirk.name: Gravity Quirk
Gravity Quirk.description:
🪐 You change the weight of what you touch.

🌱 At the start a fingertip touch floats a person or object up to about a car's weight until you release it, or drags someone you grab to their knees.
📈 With training: debris dropped on cue, rubble lifted off survivors, drifting wall leaps, unshakable anchors, one-handed car throws, crushing fields, a building held aloft.
⚠️ Whatever you float falls when you let go.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Bodily Toll, as nausea and dizziness build with the weight you change.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Ochaco Uraraka (Zero Gravity).

📈 Grants: Technique +1, Quirk Control +10, Quirk Output +10, Search and Rescue +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Liftoff Tap, Ballast Palm
Gravity Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the user changes the weight of what a bare fingertip or palm touches. At first: floats people and objects up to about a ton total (a small car) until a release gesture from anywhere in sight, or makes a held person about twice as heavy for a few seconds. More needs learned techniques. Limits: skin contact only, so full gloves block it; floated things keep momentum (a pushed car still hits hard) and drift in wind. Past the total, new touches do nothing; no push or pull at range; all of it falls if the user lets go or is knocked out. Quirk Strain: light: floating one person or object; moderate: making someone heavy, floating debris or rubble, drifting leap; heavy: anchoring something, throwing a car; severe: signature crush, holding up a collapsing building. Type: Emitter. Law: floating a person against their will is unlawful restraint; the user is liable for anything floated that falls on someone. Look: touched things rise shimmering or sag floorward.

Elasticity Quirk.name: Elasticity Quirk
Elasticity Quirk.description:
🪀 You make surfaces, and even the air, elastic.

🌱 At the start a touch turns a door-sized patch of floor, wall or air into a stretching sheet that stops a blow and throws it back, or springs you a story up.
📈 With training: nets that catch falling people, slingshot launches, holding bands, floors no enemy can stand on, truck-stopping barriers, a dome that returns every blow.
⚠️ Allies need to know where your patches are.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Cognitive Fade, as holding many patches in mind wears down your focus.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Gentle Criminal (Elasticity).

📈 Grants: Intelligence +1, Quirk Control +10, Quirk Mobility +10, Acrobatics +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Bounceback Sheet, Springstep
Elasticity Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the user touches a surface, or swipes air within reach, and makes it elastic: it gives under force and snaps back. A new adult user keeps a few door-sized patches; a surface patch lasts about a minute, an air patch a few seconds, unless dropped sooner. Bigger feats need techniques. Limits: at the start a patch only returns the force put in; it stops bodies and objects, not fire, light, gas, sound or electricity; bullets or a speeding car tear through. Allies hitting an unknown patch are thrown too. Never works on living bodies or worn clothing. Quirk Strain: light: single patch, bounce; moderate: catching net, slingshot launch, holding band; heavy: elastic floor, vehicle barrier; severe: signature snap, dome over a scene. Type: Emitter. Law: a patch left in public counts as a hidden trap; the user answers for anyone hurt by one they forgot to release. Look: in use, touched surfaces ripple; elastic air is a faint warp, plain in rain, dust or smoke.

Creation Quirk.name: Creation Quirk
Creation Quirk.description:
🧰 You make solid, nonliving objects out of your own skin, built from your body's stored reserves.

🌱 At the start you pull simple things of one or two materials from your palms and arms: a staff, a baton, a rope, a shield you can crouch behind.
📈 With training: tangling bolas, field medical supplies, a spring grapple, a steel dome, sleeping-gas canisters, a ring of cannons and, at the top, whole working machines.
⚠️ You can only make what you have studied.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Finite Fuel, since every object costs what you have eaten.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Momo Yaoyorozu (Creation).

📈 Grants: Intelligence +1, Quirk Control +10, Quirk Stamina +10, Science +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Palm Forge, Bulwark Shield
Creation Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the user makes solid, nonliving objects that push out through the skin, built from stored body fat. A new adult user makes a simple one- or two-material object, baton to crouch-behind shield, in a second or two; a key or spring takes a quiet minute. Objects are real and stay. Bigger feats need techniques. Limits: only what the user has studied down to its materials; a guess comes out brittle or fails. At the start, nothing alive, at a distance or bigger than the user. A dozen batons leave a new user hungry and shaky; made food never repays its cost; enemies can take made things. Quirk Strain: light: handheld tool or weapon; moderate: shield, bolas, medical supplies, grapple; heavy: shelter dome, gas canister; severe: signature move, large machine. Type: Emitter. Law: a made blade or gun is still a weapon; a made ID or banknote is forgery. Look: in use, skin glows faintly (player's color) where objects emerge, so costumes bare the arms or back.

Plant Quirk.name: Plant Quirk
Plant Quirk.description:
🌿 You grow living vines from your body and raise roots from the ground.

🌱 At the start your vines reach about ten meters, hold an adult and bind limbs, a thorned vine whips anyone in reach, and crops you touch grow days' worth in minutes.
📈 With training: thorn hedges across a street, buried people found through roots, vine swings, lifting rubble, a hardwood ram and, at the top, every plant in a city block.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Stamina Drain, since every vine grows from your body and needs water and sunlight to regrow.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Ibara Shiozaki (Vines), Kamui Woods (Arbor).

📈 Grants: Endurance +1, Quirk Control +10, Quirk Output +10, Survival +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Tendril Bind, Thorn Lash
Plant Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the user grows vines from the skin, usually forearms or scalp, and raises roots from touched soil. A new adult user sends wrist-thick vines about ten meters in a second or two, able to hold an adult, and grows touched crops days' worth in minutes. Bigger feats need techniques. Limits: fire burns vines, blades cut them; cut vines die, and regrowth needs water and sunlight, so long fights in dark, dry places starve it. Roots need soil or cracked ground; at the start the user cannot command plants they did not grow. Quirk Strain: light: tendril, lash; moderate: hedge, root listening, swing line; heavy: lifting rubble, hardwood ram; severe: signature move, a block's plants. Type: Emitter (also fits Mutant). Law: unlicensed binding is unlawful restraint; roots that crack a foundation are property damage. Look: thorned vines push from the skin, roots crack up through soil; as a Mutant Quirk, a permanent feature (vines in hair, bark on forearms).

Earth Quirk.name: Earth Quirk
Earth Quirk.description:
🪨 You shape stone, concrete and packed soil by touch.

🌱 At the start you tip up a chest-high slab for cover, drive a stone spur under an attacker, cut steps into a wall and move a car's weight of ground in a second or two.
📈 With training: feet locked in the floor, a ridge heaving down a street, a rising column, shoring a collapse while you open a way in, crushing walls, a reshaped block.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Recoil, as every push into the ground jars your wrists.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Cementoss (Cement), Pixie-Bob (Earth Flow).

📈 Grants: Power +1, Quirk Control +10, Quirk Output +10, Search and Rescue +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Upturned Slab, Stone Spur
Earth Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the user shapes stone, concrete, brick and packed soil by touch; it softens, flows where pushed, sets hard on release. At first: about a car's weight within a few meters in a second or two (chest-high slab, spur that throws an adult, steps up a wall). Shapes are real stone and stay. More needs learned techniques. Limits: the user must touch or stand on the material, moving only what is joined to it; metal, wood, glass and flesh do not answer (useless on a steel deck or in the air). Shaping takes a moment; reshaping a load-bearing wall can drop a building. Quirk Strain: light: slab, spur; moderate: gripping feet, a ridge down a street, a rising column; heavy: shoring a building, crushing vise; severe: signature move, reshaping a block. Type: Emitter. Law: unlicensed reshaping of roads or buildings is property damage; sealing a person in is unlawful confinement. Look: none at rest; ground ripples from the palms, gray grit climbs the wrists, stone grinds up.

Magnetism Quirk.name: Magnetism Quirk
Magnetism Quirk.description:
🧲 You pull and push iron and steel, and you can give anything you touch a magnetic pole.

🌱 At the start you snatch a knife or a gun out of a hand from about ten meters, stop a thrown wrench in midair and slap an attacker away with a repelling push.
📈 With training: marked people locked to walls or each other, scrap storms, girder rides, falling beams caught, a car swung through a barricade, all the steel in a block.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Loss of Control, as a strained field grabs metal you never meant to move.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Magne (Magnetism).

📈 Grants: Technique +1, Quirk Control +10, Quirk Output +10, Combat Tactics +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Iron Snatch, Repulse Burst
Magnetism Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the user pulls and pushes iron, steel and anyone or anything marked by touch. A new adult user moves steel within about ten meters, up to a person's weight (a knife, a manhole cover). Marks keep a user-picked pole for the scene; opposite marks within a few meters slam together, matching ones push apart. More needs techniques. Limits: aluminum, copper, plastic, wood, stone and unmarked flesh ignore it; most bullets (lead, copper) pass through. The user must see targets; the field wipes cards and scrambles nearby phones; scrap driven edge-first maims and is lethal force. Quirk Strain: light: snatch, shove; moderate: locking marks, scrap volley, glide; heavy: catching falling steel, swinging a car; severe: signature move, a block's steel. Type: Emitter. Law: hurling metal at people without a license is assault with a weapon; disrupting a pacemaker is endangering life. Look: loose metal twitches toward the user, a low hum, marks glow faintly, one color per pole.

Acid Quirk.name: Acid Quirk
Acid Quirk.description:
🧪 You secrete acid from your skin and set its strength and thickness each time, from a harmless sting to acid that eats rope, plastic and wood.

🌱 At the start you spray it a few meters, make an attacker drop their weapon with a sting and skate on a slick film faster than you can run.
📈 With training: melted locks and car doors, glued feet, etched climbing routes, an unholdable coat, armor-ruining rain and, at the top, dissolving only what you name.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Bodily Toll, as overuse leaves your skin raw.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Mina Ashido (Acid).

📈 Grants: Speed +1, Quirk Output +10, Quirk Mobility +10, Acrobatics +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Sizzle Flick, Slick Skate
🛡️ Resists: corrosive
Acid Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the user secretes acid from the skin, mostly palms and soles, setting strength and thickness each time: stinging film, sticky gel, or acid that eats rope, plastic and wood in seconds. A new adult user sprays it a few meters, about a bucket's worth before running dry; their skin resists corrosives. Bigger feats need techniques. Limits: water dilutes it, baking soda neutralizes it, it pools where it runs; fumes in a closed room sting everyone's eyes and lungs, allies included. It eats thick steel or concrete only slowly; full strength scars skin for life, so restraint is the skill. Quirk Strain: light: spray, skating film; moderate: glob, melted lock, etched climb; heavy: full-body coat, acid rain; severe: signature move, tuned solvent. Type: Emitter. Law: acid thrown at a person is aggravated assault; melting locks or cars unlicensed is burglary or property damage. Look: skin glistens with hissing fluid (player's color); skating leaves a wet, shining trail.

Toxic Gas Quirk.name: Toxic Gas Quirk
Toxic Gas Quirk.description:
☁️ Your body brews gas and lets it out through your breath or your skin.

🌱 At the start you spit a stinging irritant into a foe's face and fill a room with thick, harmless smoke that hides you and the people you protect.
📈 With training: sleep gas, trace gas that finds survivors in rubble, crowd-flooring nausea, a smothered fire, gas through masks, a building put to sleep with no one hurt.
⚠️ Gas hits whoever breathes it, so where you release it matters most.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Bodily Toll, as your lungs and throat burn raw.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Mustard (Gas).

📈 Grants: Intelligence +1, Quirk Output +10, Quirk Control +10, Stealth +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Bitter Breath, Smoke Pall
🛡️ Resists: toxic
Toxic Gas Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: the user exhales body-made gas (or sweats it from the palms), one blend per release; at the start, stinging irritant or thick harmless smoke. A new adult user fills a room about five meters wide in a few seconds or sends a jet a few strides; a cloud lingers a few minutes in still air. Own gas never harms them. Knockout and stronger blends need techniques. Limits: wind, rain and water spray scatter it; sealed masks and held breath keep it out; it drifts onto allies, hostages and bystanders downwind. It takes a few breaths, cannot be recalled, and in a sealed room builds to a breath-stopping dose. Quirk Strain: light: irritant jet, smoke; moderate: knockout cloud, trace gas; heavy: nausea front, smothering a fire, mask-piercing dose; severe: signature storm, dosing a building. Type: Emitter. Law: unlicensed gassing is assault; licensed heroes using knockout gas in arrests answer for all who breathe it. Look: haze in the player's color, sharp or sweet smell.

Warp Quirk.name: Warp Quirk
Warp Quirk.description:
🌀 You open linked gates: step into one and out of the other.

🌱 At the start gates reach about fifty meters to a spot you can see or have stood in; small ones strike from odd angles, door-sized ones carry you and a companion out.
📈 With training: attacks sent back, peeks into sealed rooms, crowd exits, villains sent far from hostages, the city crossed in a step, command of every door in a building.
⚠️ Warp users are rare, and agencies, the Commission and villains all track them.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Cognitive Fade, as holding two places in mind wears you down.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Kurogiri (Warp Gate).

📈 Grants: Intelligence +1, Quirk Control +10, Quirk Mobility +10, Navigation +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Sidelong Reach, Threshold Step
Warp Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: two linked gates, one beside the user and one at a spot they can picture (in sight or once stood on); what enters one leaves the other. At first: about fifty meters, at most door-sized, open a few seconds, one pair at a time. More needs learned techniques. Limits: a gate takes a moment to open and works both ways, so quick foes can dodge, follow through or shoot back. Gates never open inside solid matter or a person and never cut: a closing gate pushes anything halfway through back out. Losing focus shuts every gate. Quirk Strain: light: small gates, short step; moderate: turning an attack aside, peephole, group exit; heavy: sending someone away, crossing the city; severe: signature collapse, taking every door in a building. Type: Emitter. Law: moving a person through a gate without consent is abduction; the Commission tracks every registered warp user. Look: none at rest; each gate a flat ring of swirling haze in the player's chosen color, far side visible.

Living Shadow Quirk.name: Living Shadow Quirk
Living Shadow Quirk.description:
🌑 A living shadow dwells in your body, talks with its own voice and fights beside you.

🌱 At the start it reaches about five meters, catches blows and falls meant for you or a friend, and rakes opponents with its claws.
📈 With training it pins people, hauls you up buildings, scouts under doors, digs out survivors, wraps you as armor, strikes in step with you and stays yours in total dark.
⚠️ Darkness makes it bigger, stronger and wilder; bright light shrinks it into a timid sulk.
🔗 Common drawback pairing: Loss of Control, as darkness and anger loosen your hold on it.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Fumikage Tokoyami (Dark Shadow).

📈 Grants: Cooperativeness +1, Quirk Control +10, Quirk Output +10, Team Coordination +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Shade Catch, Umbra Rake
Living Shadow Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: a shadow creature with its own mind, voice and player-picked temper lives in the user and pours from their chest. In indoor light a new adult user's shadow is user-sized, reaches about five meters, throws an adult, claws. Darkness makes it bigger, stronger, wilder; bright light (sun, floodlights, fire) shrinks it to a timid scrap.
